tightGap.title: Scheduling — after catching up
tightGap.description: After a busy week, several tasks can pile up and get done on one day. The next regular date can then land very soon after — e.g. a water change due again just 3 days later. This setting controls what happens:
tightGap.calmDesc: Skip the next regular date if it falls within the threshold of the interval — you just did the task, after all. Exactly one date is skipped, the grid continues normally afterwards.
tightGap.strictDesc: Keep every regular date exactly on the grid, even shortly after a catch-up. Choose this if you want maximum consistency.
tightGap.skipWithin: Skip when the next date is within
tightGap.footnote: Applies to all plans. Individual plans can still override this in their edit dialog.

streak.title: Day streak
body: Days in a row without neglected care. A day counts when nothing was left behind by more than one full interval — so days with nothing due count too.
Feeding never breaks it, and neither does a task the app re-planned to your next preferred day.
Today only counts once everything due today is done. Until then you are looking at yesterday's number.

behindKpi.title: What counts as behind
body: A task is behind once its target date has passed — the date it was originally due, not the date shown on its card.
The target date never moves. That is what keeps your backlog honest while the app keeps re-planning the visible date for you.

adherence.title: Adherence over 30 days
body: Across all your plans: the share of planned occurrences you closed on time in the last 30 days.
On time means on the target day or within one day of it. From 80 % it reads as on track.

onTime.title: % on time
body: For this plan alone: how many of its occurrences you closed on the target day or within one day of it, over the last 30 days.
It appears once the plan has at least one completed occurrence in that window.

plannedDate.title: Behind, but planned for a later date?
body: Those are two different dates, and both are true.
The target date is when the task was due. It never moves, so your backlog stays honest.
The date on the card is where the app has re-planned it: your next preferred weekday. It is recalculated every day and never written down.
So “behind 2d · planned Saturday” means it was due two days ago, and Saturday is the next day you would actually do it.

earlyLater.title: Done early and Later
body: Done early logs the task now and starts the next interval from today.
Later moves only this one occurrence. The target date stays put, so a task that was behind still counts as behind — and a calendar you subscribed to moves the event instead of adding a second one.

cyclingState.title: Cycling or established
body: While a tank is cycling, nitrite and ammonia peaks are part of the process. Aquaman judges them more leniently and the coach reads them in that light.
Switch to established once the tank has settled. From then on any nitrite above zero is treated as a real warning again.

cyclingDay.title: Cycling day and the NO₂ trend
body: The day is counted from when you created this tank in Aquaman, not from when you filled it.
The arrow compares your newest nitrite reading with the oldest of the last three. Falling is what you want to see.

nh3.title: Free ammonia (NH₃)
body: This value is calculated, not measured. Your test kit reads total ammonium (NH₄); how much of it is actually the toxic free ammonia depends on pH and temperature.
The same NH₄ reading is harmless at pH 6.5 and dangerous at pH 8.2. That is why Aquaman judges the calculated NH₃ and not the raw number.
From 0.012 mg/l you get a warning, above 0.02 mg/l it is critical.

tightInterval.title: Interval too tight?
body: This shows up once three of the plan's preferred days have passed since its target date — the task would have come around three times.
It is a suggestion, not a reproach. Often the interval is simply shorter than your routine, and widening it is the honest fix.

aiData.title: What the coach can see
body: Your data only: tank profiles, water tests including the calculated NH₃, your care history and how far behind you are.
Never your API keys, your calendar or MCP tokens, your .env contents or any server path.
It can draft changes but never write them. Every proposal waits for your confirmation.

planReview.title: The coach badge
body: A pulsing dot means the coach is reviewing your plan, triggered by changed tank data or new water values.
A number means it finished and has that many suggestions waiting for you.

medianDelay.title: Median delay
body: Per action type, the middle value of how late your completions were: half were quicker, half slower.
The median rather than the average, because a single forgotten fortnight would otherwise skew the whole picture.

notes.waterRanges: Target ranges come from the water type and can be overridden per tank. In an established tank the nitrite target is 0.
notes.sparkline: The last six tests, oldest to newest.
notes.preferredDays: Occurrences only land on these days — including when the app re-plans an overdue one.
notes.endsOn: After this date the plan disappears from dashboard, calendar and feed. Your logs stay.
notes.aiGate: The coach drafts. Nothing reaches your data until you confirm it.
notes.aiLimits: There is a daily budget for both calls and tokens. Both reset at local midnight.
notes.aiOffline: Without an API key every other part of Aquaman works as normal.
notes.costUnits: An estimate derived from token prices, not an amount in any currency.
notes.timezone: “Today” follows the timezone Aquaman is configured with, not your browser clock.
notes.plansStat: Active care plans, including those with nothing due this week.
notes.feedMax: Up to five feedings per day.

concepts.title: How Aquaman plans
concepts.lede: One idea explains most of what you see on the dashboard: Aquaman keeps two dates for every task, and only one of them ever moves.

sections.heading: Two dates, both true
body: Every occurrence has a target date — when it was due. It is set once, when the occurrence is created, and then never moves.
What you see on a card is the planned date: where the app suggests you actually do it. If the target date has passed, the planned date moves forward to your next preferred weekday.
A card reading “behind 2d · planned Saturday” is telling you both at once: it was due two days ago, and Saturday is the realistic next slot.

sections.heading: Re-planning is never written down
body: The planned date is recalculated every time something reads it, and never stored. Only what you do is recorded: completing a task, or pushing it back with Later.
That is why your subscribed calendar is always current even if you never open the dashboard — and why a week of ignoring the app does not quietly rewrite its own history.

sections.heading: Why the backlog stays honest
body: Because the target date never moves, being behind cannot disappear by itself. The app keeps offering you a realistic next date without pretending the delay did not happen.
Aquaman also counts how many of your preferred days went by since the target date. Once three have passed, it asks whether the interval is simply too tight — a question, not a telling-off.

sections.heading: Preferred days
body: Each plan has the weekdays you are willing to do it on. New occurrences are placed on one of those days from the start, so you never begin a task already late by construction.
Re-planning respects them too: an overdue weekend task moves to the next weekend, not to Tuesday.

sections.heading: Why calendar events move instead of doubling
body: In the ICS feed each occurrence keeps a stable identity tied to its target date. When the planned date changes, the event moves.
If the identity followed the planned date instead, Google would delete and recreate the event every day you stayed behind — losing your reminders and flashing duplicates in between.

sections.heading: Feeding is not a plan
body: Feeding is a daily habit with its own control on the dashboard. It is never an occurrence, never appears in the calendar or the feed, and never affects whether you are behind.
You can log up to five feedings a day and fill in a day you forgot, up to 30 days back.

offline.title: No contact
offline.subtitle: The app cannot reach your server right now
offline.body: Aquaman keeps your tanks, schedules and water values on your own server — so there is nothing to show while the connection is down.
offline.hint: Check your Wi-Fi or VPN, then try again. Nothing is lost: anything you saved before is safely on the server.
